headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but Great Expectations can read files while LlamaFactory is a local-only, non-file agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations exposes file I/O for data sources and validation results, but LlamaFactory has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or browser surfaces. With no shared communication channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Great Expectations outputs into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared prompt channels.
Do not paste validation output into LlamaFactory without sanitizing it.
Use a separate review step for any text copied between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, while LlamaFactory is local-only with no file read/write or network egress. A leakage path exists only if sensitive data is placed into Great Expectations files and then manually transferred; the blast radius is limited because LlamaFactory cannot exfiltrate by default.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in Great Expectations-managed files and then copied into LlamaFactory prompts, leakage risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later given filesystem or network access, the severity should be re-evaluated upward.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or PHI in validation artifacts.
Store test datasets in a redacted sandbox.
Review any copied text before moving it between tools.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and work with files, but LlamaFactory cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping write authority on the same mutable resource in the profiles, so conflict is limited to unusual external orchestration.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped with additional tooling that adds write or git permissions, reassess.
mitigations: Keep git operations outside both agents.
Run package installation only in a controlled environment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation, but LlamaFactory has no documented downstream action-taking authority or automatic trust pipeline. Without an explicit orchestrator that treats Great Expectations output as authoritative, cascading error is not a default-path problem.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds Great Expectations outputs directly into LlamaFactory without verification, cascading error becomes more plausible.
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate customer-facing responses from those outputs, impact increases.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before reuse of validation output.
Require schema checks on any transferred artifacts.
Label Great Expectations outputs as advisory, not authoritative.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: both agents are open-source, docs-only, and list no secrets handled, OAuth scopes, or data residency constraints. Great Expectations touches validation data, but LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no network egress, so a residency or certification breach is not supported here.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Great Expectations workflows, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdictional or certification constraint not shown in the profiles, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair by default.
Document any residency or retention requirements before deployment.
Review access logs if sensitive datasets are later introduced.
